title: scientific-evidence-gate dependency graph
description: graph.json declares artifacts (nodes) and what derives from what (edges [parent, child]). This schema is documentation: validation is implemented in science_gate/dependencies.py, which additionally refuses duplicate node ids, two nodes naming the same file (case-insensitively on Windows), a node naming a file the tool writes (graph-state.json, impact-report.json, revalidation-report.json beside the graph), edges naming undeclared nodes, repeated edges, a history that does not end in the node's declared validity, and malformed JSON (duplicate keys, NaN, Infinity). A cycle is an ERROR (GRAPH_CYCLE), as is a node path that could leave the manifest directory (UNSAFE_PATH). Other defects are MALFORMED_GRAPH. Node paths are relative to the manifest's directory, not to the graph file. The tool never rewrites graph.json; state it derives is written to graph-state.json ($defs/graph_state).

schema.description: Optional. When present it must be science-gate-graph/v1.

utc_timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC with a Z suffix.

validity.description: SUPERSEDED and INVALIDATED are declared by people; the tool never sets them and detection and impact walks keep them. STALE_PENDING_REVALIDATION and UNRESOLVED are pending.

path.description: The artifact's file, relative to the manifest directory, or null for an artifact without a file (it can then never be re-hashed, only cleared by early cutoff).

recorded_sha256.description: The digest the artifact was established with. Must be null when path is null. A file without a recorded digest (NO_BASELINE) keeps the graph from passing until it is revalidated.

history.description: Declared history. When non-empty, its last entry's 'to' must equal validity.

edge.description: [parent, child]: child is derived from parent.

transition.description: One change of validity. The contract's {at, from, to, reason}; the tool also writes trigger (the node whose change caused it) and the recorded digest before and after, so original and corrected states are both preserved.

state_transition.description: A transition as the tool writes it into graph-state.json: every key present.

graph_state.description: graph-state.json, written beside graph.json by 'impact' and 'revalidate' through a safe write. For a node with tool history the state is authoritative (the last history entry must match its validity and recorded digest). For a node without, graph.json's declaration applies. A state file that exists but cannot be read or validated is never ignored: commands stop with ERROR and the check ABSTAINs with PROTOCOL_BROKEN.

stale_because.description: Pending direct parents, plus the node itself when its own file changed or its pending state was declared. Early cutoff clears a node only when this becomes empty.

impact_report.description: impact-report.json or revalidation-report.json, written beside graph-state.json. The same content is printed as markdown after the headline and the written paths. Secret-looking values are redacted.

blocked.description: true while a CONCLUSION or FIGURE_OR_TABLE is STALE_PENDING_REVALIDATION; false only when the graph is fully current; null when it cannot be decided.

impact.description: Present for 'impact': origin and descendants (id, kind, depth, path_from_changed_node, prior_state, state, publication_node).

revalidate.description: Present for 'revalidate': outcome (REVALIDATED_UNCHANGED, REVALIDATED_CHANGED, REFUSED_UPSTREAM_PENDING, NO_FILE_TO_HASH, FILE_UNAVAILABLE), digests before and after, cleared and still-pending descendants.
